record.paper_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
record.original_question: In the ring of bounded analytic functions on the unit ball or the polydisc in n variables, is the intersection of two finitely-generated ideals again finitely generated? This was proved for n = 1 by McVoy and Rubel [559]. (L. A. Rubel)

evidence.quote: In the ring of bounded analytic functions on the unit ball or the polydisc in n variables, is the intersection of two finitely-generated ideals again finitely generated?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$, and let $\Omega$ denote either the open unit ball $B_n = \{z \in \mathbb{C}^n : \|z\| < 1\}$ or the open unit polydisc $D^n = \{z \in \mathbb{C}^n : |z_j| < 1 \text{ for } j=1,\dots,n\}$. Let $H^\infty(\Omega)$ be the commutative unital ring of bounded holomorphic functions $f : \Omega \to \mathbb{C}$, equipped with pointwise addition and multiplication. A commutative ring $R$ is called coherent if, for every pair of finitely generated ideals $I, J \subseteq R$, the intersection $I \cap J$ is again a finitely generated ideal of $R$.

Question: Is $H^\infty(\Omega)$ coherent? Equivalently, is it true that for every pair of finitely generated ideals $I, J$ in $H^\infty(\Omega)$, the ideal $I \cap J$ is finitely generated?

(For $n = 1$, in the ring $H^\infty(\mathbb{D})$ of bounded holomorphic functions on the unit disc, the intersection of two finitely generated ideals is known to be finitely generated.)
artifact.category_tag: Bounded analytic functions and coherent rings
artifact.status_search_result: Mortini and Wick (arXiv:1606.05568, "Noncoherent uniform algebras in C^n") prove that for n ≥ 2 the algebra H^∞ of bounded holomorphic functions on the unit ball and on the polydisc in C^n is not coherent; equivalently, there exist finitely generated ideals whose intersection is not finitely generated. This resolves the question negatively in dimensions ≥ 2.

status_evidence.title: Noncoherent uniform algebras in C^n
status_evidence.snippet: The authors give a sufficient criterion for non-coherence and apply it to show that the ball algebra and H^∞ on the ball/polydisc are not coherent for n ≥ 2.
status_evidence.claim: H^∞(B_n) and H^∞(D^n) are not coherent for n ≥ 2, so the intersection of two finitely generated ideals need not be finitely generated.
